_comment: Host-specific BLFS review decisions for `laptop`. Merged on top of the shared recipes/blfs-overrides.json by bin/extract-blfs.py, page by page and block by block.

3.reason:
Requested 2026-09-01: no root login for ssh. Reverts the shared override (recipes/blfs-overrides.json), which sets 'yes' -- correct for server's original bootstrap situation (root-only, no other account existed yet, described in that override's own reason) but not this host: john already has full wheel/sudo access from the start (blfs-adduser-john, seq 14.5), so there is no window where root-over-SSH is the only way in. This is also the book's own unmodified default (block 3's real text is 'PermitRootLogin no' -- confirmed directly against book/blfs-13.0/postlfs/openssh.html).

sed -i prefix added after a real bug: the book's own `>>` is append-only, and sshd_config already had a 'PermitRootLogin yes' line from this step's first build (under the old shared override) still present when this override's own line got appended on top -- sshd honors the FIRST occurrence of a repeated directive, so the stale 'yes' silently won even after this fix was written. Caught by direct inspection of the built config (`grep '^PermitRootLogin ' /etc/ssh/sshd_config` should always show exactly one line after this step; two means this same bug recurred), not assumed correct from a clean build log. Idempotent now: strips any existing line for this directive before appending, safe across any number of --force reruns.

5.reason: Requested 2026-09-01: no password login for ssh. Shared override drops this block because 'No authorized_keys exists on this system, so applying it together with the block above would leave no way to log in at all' -- no longer true here: hosts/laptop/recipes/blfs-authorized-keys-john.sh (seq 186) installs john's real authorized_keys, carried over from the live host, before this takes effect. Key-only auth from here on; PermitRootLogin no above means root can't even attempt a password login regardless. Not idempotency-guarded like block 3 above: this was the first time either directive was written (nothing to duplicate against) -- if this step is ever --force rerun again, re-check for the same append-duplication risk before trusting it blindly.

2.reason:
Driver scope is bound to this machine's GPU, so it lives here rather than in the shared file -- same reason blfs-mesa is a host recipe on server.

gallium-drivers=iris (book default: auto). This box's GPU is Intel HD Graphics 520 (Skylake GT2, Gen9) -- iris is the modern Gen8+ Mesa driver (crocus is for Gen4-7, not this hardware). auto would build every vendor's driver (AMD, NVIDIA/nouveau, virgl, svga) this hardware will never use.

vulkan-drivers=intel (book default: auto). Mesa's ANV driver officially supports this GPU generation -- real Vulkan, not the swrast/lavapipe-or-nothing situation server's Kepler card faced. auto would again pull in every vendor.

No gallium-opencl flag: an earlier version of this override tried '-D gallium-opencl=disabled' to dodge a libclc dependency, but that option name doesn't exist in this mesa version's meson.options at all ('Unknown option') -- real failure 2026-08-30. The actual cause: mesa's own meson.build makes gallium-drivers=iris and vulkan-drivers=intel unconditionally require libclc (src: with_driver_using_cl, unrelated to rusticl/OpenCL as a feature toggle -- iris/anv's own shader compilation pipeline needs it). Fixed properly by building the real dependency chain instead of fighting it: llvm (hand-authored, shared recipe, skips the book's PAM-dependent test suite) -> spirv-llvm-translator -> libclc, added to packages.py ahead of this step. Confirmed with the operator before committing to that ~4-hour addition given tight disk headroom at the time.

glvnd=enabled, REVERSED 2026-08-31 from an earlier glvnd=disabled call. Original reasoning: single GPU vendor, nothing to dispatch between, so libglvnd seemed skippable. That reasoning didn't survive contact with real Hyprland-ecosystem builds: aquamarine's CMakeLists links against OpenGL::OpenGL, the GLVND-specific target CMake's FindOpenGL only creates when a real libOpenGL.so (GLVND's own dispatch library) is present -- confirmed via a real CMake configure failure ('links to OpenGL::OpenGL ... but the target was not found'), independent of how many GPU vendors are actually installed. GLVND turns out to be the expected baseline this class of package assumes, not an optional multi-vendor extra -- libglvnd built (packages.py, right before this step) and mesa's own glvnd option switched to match.

platforms=x11,wayland is the book default and is kept deliberately, unlike server's now-moot copy of the same line: this machine actually runs both, natively Wayland via Hyprland and X11 via XWayland for compat.

3.reason: Operator-requested (2026-09-04). REVISED same day after a real failed attempt: an earlier version of this override used `-submodules qtdeclarative,qtsvg,qtshadertools,qtwayland,qtmultimedia` on the theory that it was an opt-in whitelist replacing the book's `-skip` blacklist. That theory was wrong, proven by a live build: with the tarball's full 40-module 'everywhere' tree already extracted, Qt6's top-level `-top-level` configure builds every module it finds by default regardless of `-submodules` -- confirmed by watching the actual build compile qtlanguageserver, qtquick3d, and (critically) qtwebengine, none of which were requested, and by `sudo du -sh` on the source tree showing qtwebengine at 4.6G already extracted mid-build. Killed at 4089/8050 build steps, 17.3GB free (down from 34GB), before a full Chromium-embedded build could make things worse. `-submodules` apparently only forces a module ON if it would otherwise be auto-disabled by a missing optional dependency -- it is not an exclusive filter. `-skip` (the book's own proven mechanism, already used for 3 modules in the unmodified recipe) is what actually excludes a module from the build; this override now lists every module except the 5 Quickshell/DankMaterialShell actually need (checked against DankMaterialShell's real QML source, not docs) plus the always-built qtbase -- 35 explicit `-skip` flags rather than 3, extending the book's own approach rather than replacing it with an untested mechanism a second time. Also added an explicit `-j` flag directly to the `ninja` invocation (2026-09-04, retry): confirmed live that bare `ninja` ignores the driver's exported `MAKEFLAGS` entirely and falls back to its own default heuristic (nproc+2 = 6 concurrent compiles on this 4-thread host) -- caught by watching `pgrep -c cc1plus` right after a retry started, before any real damage, and fixed before restarting rather than assumed correct because host.toml said jobs=2. Started at `-j4` (2026-09-04, live build): the earlier disk/memory incidents that motivated dropping qt6 to 2 jobs were caused by the untrimmed build accidentally compiling qtwebengine (a full Chromium embed), not by this trimmed 6-module set -- confirmed live, RAM usage never exceeded ~3GB of 15GB total even at `-j2` for the first ~50% of this trimmed build, so operator decision (2026-09-04) raised it straight to `-j4` for future runs of this specific trimmed recipe rather than working back up incrementally. The in-progress build that caught the MAKEFLAGS bug was left running at -j2 to completion rather than restarted, since ninja doesn't need MAKEFLAGS/jobs count to be right to finish correctly, just to finish efficiently.

6.reason: Installs icons/desktop entries for assistant/designer/linguist/qdbusviewer, all from qttools -- not in the trimmed -submodules list above (block 3), so qttools/src doesn't exist and this block would fail outright (`pushd: qttools/src: No such file or directory`). None of those GUI dev tools are wanted here; this project only needs Qt6 as a Quickshell/DankMaterialShell runtime dependency.
